newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi police seize large quantity of explosives.
newsitem.headline: Delhi police seize large quantity of explosives.

text.p: Indian police said on Monday they seized a large quantity of sophisticated explosives from suspected militants who they said planned to carry out bomb attacks in the capital this month.

Delhi police commissioner Nikhil Kumar told a news conference that police, on a tip-off, raided a rented house in south Delhi and found 10 kg (22 lb) of the powerful Research Developed Explosive (RDX) as well as electronic timers and detonators.
"Ten kg of rdx probably meant to cause explosions ahead of republic day has been seized from the house," Nikhil Kumar said.
Police arrested two people whom they said planned to carry out bomb attacks ahead of India's Republic Day on January 26.
The two were linked to a Dubai-based international smuggler suspected of planning a string of bomb blasts which killed 263 people in Bombay in March 1993, police said.
Authorities, fearing attacks by militant groups, have tightened security ahead of Republic Day.
